title: The Serapeum as a sonohydrogen plant

tellings.quote: ultrasound to break down water molecules to produce hydrogen and oxygen which is my hypothesis for the function of the sarapium.

plain: Geoffrey Drumm, a guest on host Jesse Michels's podcast, offers his idea about the Serapeum, an underground complex of huge stone boxes at Saqqara in Egypt. He says his hypothesis is that it used ultrasound, very high-pitched sound, to break water into hydrogen and oxygen, which would make it an ancient energy plant rather than a burial site.
